slides.title: Working order (each analytical run)
bullets: 1. Before work read the instrument manual; check that the parameters from the kit IFU are entered correctly in the programme.
2. Prepare the working reagent as the kit IFU says; warm it before use if the IFU requires (for example the ALT monoreagent to 37 °C).
3. Set the zero as in the IFU: against distilled water, air or the reagent blank.
4. Calibrate: measure the standard (calibrator) or enter the factor.

slides.title: Working order (each analytical run)
bullets: 5. Measure the control material: internal quality control is done every day in each analytical run and the result is recorded on the control chart.
6. Measure the patient samples; if a result is above the linearity, dilute the sample, repeat the determination and multiply the result by the dilution.

slides.title: Working with control material
bullets: The basis of internal control is measuring one standardised control material every day over a long period and recording the results on a control chart.
Control materials approved for use in Uzbekistan are recommended; if there are none, material made from unused sample leftovers (serum, plasma, urine) may be used.
When preparing: read the manufacturer’s instructions, open the vial carefully, measure the solvent exactly, close the cap and mix without foaming, keep to the dissolution time.
Even if the control material is stated to be free of viral hepatitis and HIV antigens, handle it with great care.

slides.title: Working with control material
bullets: Recheck a doubtful result with freshly prepared reagent and freshly prepared control material.

slides.title: Sources of error and instrument care
bullets: Errors at the measuring stage: a broken temperature regime, inaccurate dosing of samples and reagents, instrument faults and changes in the programme.
The water must be clean with a pH of 6.5–7.5; storing reagents above 37 °C sharply reduces their stability.
On the instrument side: check the parts that dose the reagents and, if needed, the calibration and programme parameters; do not use scratched cuvettes; wipe the optical system.
If possible check a doubtful result on another instrument.
Daily and weekly maintenance, the washing routine and the lamp warm-up time are not given in this manual — take them from the analyser’s user manual.

slides.title: Factors affecting the quality of biochemical tests
rows: Water clean with pH 6.5–7.5; in doubt water from another source; reagent bottle caps clean
Pipette fits the volume and is sound; correct order of work, temperature, incubation time and dosing
Solvent volume, shelf life, storage rules (storing above 37 °C sharply reduces stability)

slides.title: Factors affecting the quality of biochemical tests
rows: Solvent volume, pipette, water quality, shelf life, stability at 2–6 °C

Quality of collection; centrifuge speed and temperature; separating plasma/serum from cells; closing containers; plastic containers only; freezing a specimen kept longer than 4 hours; not testing turbid, haemolysed, lipaemic or very high-bilirubin specimens

slides.title: Factors affecting the quality of biochemical tests
rows: Calibration, programme parameters, not working in scratched cuvettes, wiping the optical system
